newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chronopost takes 33.3 pct stake in Taxi - Colis.
newsitem.headline: Chronopost takes 33.3 pct stake in Taxi - Colis.

text.p: Chronopost, the express arm of the French post office, said it had taken a 33.3 percent stake in French courier operator, Taxi-Colis following an increase in the latter's capital.

Taxi-Colis chairman, Patrice Collet, told a news conference that he and two co-managing directors now hold the remainder of the company's capital following the retirement of one of the main shareholders.
The two companies declined to disclose the size of the Chronopost investment".

"We are seeking to expand in the domestic market for urgent/same day shipments and see a good deal of overlap between ourselves and Taxi-Colis," Chronopost's chief executive officer, Frederique Tiberghien told the news conference.
There were no plans to take a controlling interest in Taxi-Colis, he added.
Taxi-Colis has an agreement with Federal Express Corp covering the movement of documents and parcels by road to Fedex's hub at Charles de Gaulle airport. The agreement runs until May 31 1998.
FedEx product services are also marketed from Taxi-Colis' distribution outlets in France.
Collet said he saw no conflict of interest between the company's agreement with FedEx and the Chronopost shareholding in Taxi-Colis.
"We would like to think there is a possibility of renewing our agreement with FedEx."
Tiberghien said: "Chronopost and FedEx are not competitors in the French domestic urgent/same day market so we see no reason for a clash."
He added: "This a niche market, ripe for development amid growing demand from customers for deadlines as short as two hours for some "just-in-time" parts and components.
Taxi-Colis' co-managing director, Renaud Duval, said there was also the potential for cooperation between both companies on a European level.
Taxi-Colis had a 1996 turnover of 320 million francs against 300 million francs in 1995. It operates a fleet of 850 road vehicles with 1,230 staff.

Chronopost, 66 percent-owned by the state post office and 34 percent by French aviation holdings group, TAT SA, recorded a 1996 turover of 2.1 billion francs, compared to 2.09 billion the previous year.
